phase: base lab environment; OIDC fixture running

steps.action: Open Settings, Advanced, Authentication: two policy cards with four switches; SSO unavailable before a provider is registered, with its help tooltip; the emergency password line
steps.expected: Legal User Authentication and Business Portal Authentication; four labelled switches; SSO disabled; tooltip text
steps.actual: The rail's Advanced group expanded to Authentication (/settings/authentication). Switches: {"Legal User Authentication":["Email and password:true","Email magic link:true","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false"],"Business Portal Authentication":["Email and password:true","Email magic link:true","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false"]}. The SSO help tooltip read "Configure an identity provider below to enable single sign-on.". The Legal card said "Administrators retain emergency password sign-in. Any required two-factor authentication still applies."

steps.action: Keep at least one sign-in method on in each card: a policy with no method is refused
steps.expected: "Enable at least one sign-in method." in both cards; stored policy unchanged
steps.actual: Observed {"Legal User Authentication":{"first":"Saved","second":"Enable at least one sign-in method.","stored":{"password":true,"magicLink":false,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}},"Business Portal Authentication":{"first":"Saved","second":"Enable at least one sign-in method.","stored":{"password":true,"magicLink":false,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}}. Email magic link was turned back on in both cards ({"legal":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false},"business":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}).

steps.action: Emergency password sign-in: Email and password off under Legal User Authentication
steps.expected: An Administrator with a password still signs in; a Legal Team Member cannot
steps.actual: With Email and password off ("Saved"), the staff page offered ["Send link","Administrator sign-in","Back to sign-in"]. Daniel (Administrator with a password) signed in with a password (me 200, role administrator). Nadia (Legal Team Member) was refused: "Password sign-in is disabled for this account." (me 401). Email and password was turned back on.

steps.expected: Links arrive; sign-ins succeed as Legal team member; rows Active; a reused link fails

steps.action: A Business User who signs in on the staff sign-in page lands in the Portal
steps.expected: Seeded Business User requests a link on /auth/login and lands under /portal
steps.actual: Felix Brandt requested a link on the staff sign-in page; opening it landed on /portal as business_user.

steps.action: Control Business Portal entry: Add northwind.example under Allowed email domains; Remove control; saved list survives reload
steps.expected: Saved; Remove northwind.example; reload keeps it
steps.actual: After Add, northwind.example appeared with a "Remove northwind.example" control and stayed after reload (["helix.example","northwind.example"]).

steps.action: A new Portal entrant on an allowed domain gets a link and a Business User account; an unapproved address gets no sign-in link or password setup link and no account
steps.expected: Allowed address becomes a Business User; unapproved address: neutral page, no mail, no account
steps.actual: doc032-bridge-auth-portal-br9976@northwind.example got "Sign in to OpenLaw", opened the Portal and is a business_user. doc032-bridge-auth-unapproved-br9976@unlisted.example saw "Helix Software Group Legal Portal Powered by OpenLaw Check your email If doc032-bridge-auth-unapproved-br9976@unlisted.e" and the neutral password-setup confirmation, but Mailpit received 0 messages and no account exists.

steps.action: A Business User sets a password through the Portal password setup link and signs in with Email and password
steps.expected: Password setup email; password sign-in reaches the Portal
steps.actual: "Set your OpenLaw password" arrived, the password was set, and Email and password sign-in on the Portal page reached /portal/onboarding as business_user.

steps.action: Remove the last allowed domain: the card shows the no-domains message; Business sign-in methods show off and all four switches are unavailable with the domain tooltip; Require two-factor authentication keeps its value; Invite user offers staff roles only
steps.expected: "No domains allowed yet. New users must be invited individually."; switches off and unavailable; tooltips; two invite roles
steps.actual: Removed ["helix.example","northwind.example"]. The card read "No domains allowed yet. New users must be invited individually." Switches ["Email and password:false:disabled","Email magic link:false:disabled","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false:disabled"] (same after reload). Stored business policy went from {"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false} to {"password":false,"magicLink":false,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}. Tooltips (no identity provider registered yet): {"Email and password":"Add an allowed email domain to enable Business User sign-in options.","Single sign-on (SSO)":"Add an allowed email domain and configure an identity provider to enable single sign-on.","Require two-factor authentication":"Add an allowed email domain to enable Business User sign-in options."}. Invite user offered ["Legal team member","Administrator"].

steps.action: After the last domain is removed: the Business Portal sign-in page shows the unavailable message; an existing Business User can no longer sign in; a session already held keeps working
steps.expected: "Sign-in is unavailable. Contact your administrator."; password sign-in refused; held session answers 200
steps.actual: The Business Portal sign-in page read "Helix Software Group Legal Portal Powered by OpenLaw Business Portal sign-in Sign-in is unavailable. The Business User session held since earlier (doc032-bridge-auth-portal-br9976@northwind.example) still answered 200 as business_user.

steps.action: To reopen the Portal, add a domain, then turn on at least one method: adding a domain does not turn the methods back on
steps.expected: After Add the switches are available but off and the Portal page stays unavailable; after turning on Email and password and Email magic link the Business User signs in again
steps.actual: After adding ["helix.example","northwind.example"] again, the switches read ["Email and password:false","Email magic link:false","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false"] (available, methods off) and the Portal page still read "Helix Software Group Legal Portal Powered by OpenLaw Business Portal sign-in Sign-in is un". Turning on Email and password ("Saved") and Email magic link ("Saved") stored {"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}, and doc032-bridge-auth-portal-pw-br9976@northwind.example signed in on the Portal page again (me 200, business_user).

steps.action: Require two-factor authentication under Business Portal Authentication keeps its value when the last domain is removed
steps.expected: On before removal; after removal the switch shows on and unavailable and the stored value stays on
steps.actual: Require two-factor authentication was turned on ("Saved"). After removing every domain the switches read ["Email and password:false:disabled","Email magic link:false:disabled","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:true:disabled"] and the stored business policy was {"password":false,"magicLink":false,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":true}. The domains ["helix.example","northwind.example"], Email and password, Email magic link and the two-factor value were restored ({"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}).

steps.actual: Turning off Email magic link showed "Saved". Opening Clara Fontaine's link sent before the change landed on /portal/login?error&method with "Helix Software Group Legal Portal Powered by OpenLaw Business Portal sign-in This sign-in link could not be used.
